book_intro:
Blue Letter Bible bakanlığı ve BLB Enstitüsü, Kutsal Yazıların tahrif edilemezliğine olan kesin inancı da içeren tarihsel, muhafazakar Hristiyan inancına bağlıdır. BLB tarafından sağlanan metin ve ses içeriği çeşitli Evanjelik gelenekleri temsil ettiğinden, kaynak materyallerde aktarılan tüm fikir ve ilkelerin bu bakanlık tarafından toplamda onaylanması gerekmez.

Blue Letter Kutsal Kitap çalışma araçları Kutsal Kitap'ı okumayı, araştırmayı ve çalışmayı kolay ve ödüllendirici hale getirir.

notes.text: Loosely adapted from 2 Kings 11:21–12:21, supplemented with the Chronicler’s own material (see 2 Chron. 24:27).
Joash did what was right. See note on 2 Kings 12:2–3.
got for him two wives. Jehoiada acts to ensure that the Davidic line will continue after being nearly destroyed by Athaliah.
restore. Athaliah and her family had defiled and damaged the temple (v. 7).
2 Chron. 24:5–6, 9 repair the house of your God. See note on 2 Kings 12:4–5.
all the people rejoiced and brought their tax. See 1 Chron. 29:6–9. The Chronicler wants his readers to see God’s service at the temple not as a burden but as a joyful duty (see Ex. 36:2–7).
The revival of temple worship lasted all the days of Jehoiada. After Jehoiada dies and is no longer there to guide him, Joash becomes spiritually unfaithful.
Jehoiada’s burial among the kings is unique for a high priest. the king listened to them. Without Jehoiada’s influence, Joash follows evil advice.
Judah’s defeat by the smaller Syrian army is a sign of divine judgment.
